searchText: <@383836935480803339> I would support adding escalator. I don't think 1559 should be delayed for it though. Whichever is ready first goes in first, whichever is ready second goes in second. How is the escalator EIP coming along? > <@383836935480803339> I would support adding escalator. I don't think 1559 should be delayed for it though. Whichever is ready first goes in first, whichever is ready second goes in second. <@301186049323958275> how does that work? they are not obviously commutative, nor even composable, as we discussed above I thought the conclusion of our discussion was that they are? I don't see any conflict between them, nor any dependency. Side note: Would be good to get the escalator EIP merged with an EIP number so it shows up on EIPs website. Base _fee is set by the protocol. Youd have an escalator with one step 🤔 1559 still lets the transaction specify fee. The escalator effects the *transaction*. If 1559 goes in first then Escalator would need to be reworded a bit, but it is a minor change. Right now a transaction has a `gasPrice`. With 1559 it would have `gasPremium, maxFee`. Escalator pre-1559 would make `gasPrice` be a function of time. Escalator post-1559 would make `gasPremium` and `maxFee` be a function of time. My thought is that escalator is much smaller in scope, so if 1559 ends up ready before escalator (even if escalator work only started officially tomorrow), it means we didn't commit very much time to the escalator implementation. I think we *should* prioritize escalator since it seems uncontroversially better than current state and is likely to have an immediate impact towards improving the user experience. Unfortunately I can't commit to helping with the work so I'm only asking as an ethereum user Step 1 is getting escalator EIP merged as draft. 😉 > Unfortunately I can't commit to helping with the work so I'm only asking as an ethereum user Sadly, this is my current state with regards to several EIPs as well. 😢 I have been thinking lately of quitting all other work and just going full-time on getting some EIPs pushed through... but the work sounds... painful. > Right now a transaction has a `gasPrice`. With 1559 it would have `gasPremium, maxFee`. Escalator pre-1559 would make `gasPrice` be a function of time. Escalator post-1559 would make `gasPremium` and `maxFee` be a function of time. <@!301186049323958275> why would maxfee be a function of time? this seems like the one parameter that should be fixed, to commit to a transaction that never costs more than some limit I set The "function of time" can include a max. it's possible the combination works, but I am simply saying that it's not obvious, and several designs exist too i Example function: `x > now + 60 ? max_fee : base_fee + block.timestamp - base_time` i'd like to write these designs down just so that we have a starting point I left a couple of comments on the EIP, I don't know the steps to getting an EIP merged though > <@!383836935480803339> I would support adding escalator. I don't think 1559 should be delayed for it though. Whichever is ready first goes in first, whichever is ready second goes in second. <@!301186049323958275> EIP-1559 implementation is ready in Geth and Besu. All parameters have been made configurable so that we can try different configurations and find the optimal parameters. What are the next steps to setup a testnet ? <@574864862338088960> From me *personally* the next steps for 1559 is to accept my PR to change it. 😄 I'm *against* 1559 right now (but not for the reason most people are). I have an open PR to resolve the issue I have with it, but I cannot merge it without agreement from 1559 authors. Once that is "dealt with" (either by silencing me, convincing me I'm wrong, or moving forward despite my disagreement) then I think getting it into OpenEthereum and Nethermind would be valuable, or if not creating a new Geth + Besu testnet. Though, I think the "right" next step is probably to put it up for discussion during an All Core Devs call. Where is your PR micah? https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/2635 <@!187490121698770945> Thanks My concern with giving miners a lever to change the target gas size is miners are very motivated to manipulate the base_fee to as close to zero as possible. I do agree with the rider concern. Making the decision explicit would also help avoid confusion. <@!187490121698770945> Do you believe there is some profitable attack vector that can be exploited by miners to drive the base_fee down? Prior to submitting that PR I asked around to see if anyone had a legitimate reason why block size needs to not be controlled by miners in order for 1559 to work and couldn't find an answer, but a solid attack vector would certainly be a valid reason for me to drop my PR and my concern about riders in 1559. some (very) preliminary notes here. not addressing any potential incentives issue nor whether any of these designs actually achieve what we like them to do, but these are already three different ways to implement a combination (there are certainly more) https://github.com/ethereum/rig/blob/master/eip1559/combination.md from my point of view the "floating escalator" seems the most reasonable (it can default to eip 1559-style txs, for one), though I worry that it might not be so easy to analyse given the interaction with basefee Why does 1559 have a separate FEECAP and GAS_PREMIUM? It feels entirely unnecessary. The one exception is when you want `block.coinbase` to pay the fee, but I don't feel like solving for that is necessary or wort the added overhead of having separate variables. It seems to me that users should specify `FEECAP` (which we can just call `GASPRICE`), and `BASEFEE` is burned and remainder goes to the miner. apart from the burning of basefee, that's not very different from a first price auction from the point of view of the user the point of having two parameters is that your bid is indexed on basefee and you have an upper bound in case basefee goes too high Hmm, I see. The idea is that you can add padding in for base fee movements *without* having to pay more to miners than they normally ask. "I'm willing to pay any BASE_FEE because I trust the algos to not try to screw me, but I'll only pay 1 neth per gas to miners, because I know that is the going rate and if I offer more they'll demand more." kinda! i would say more "i am willing to pay basefee because that's the going rate, given the demand" but yes the idea is that the premium can be relatively constant that is, if we don't believe miners collude to push the basefee to very low levels I didn't previously realize those two were separate. I now better understand why it is "not obvious" how escalator and 1559 interact. (I still think it is very possible for them to interact). I do not believe there is a profitable strategy to push the base fee down, even for miners colluding. The one exception *may* be if *all* miners collude.
